label: Otter 8x8
generated: measured off the rig source by hand-transcription with per-value provenance; flotation numbers integrated numerically off the same station profiles the bake lathes

frame.origin: ground-centre of the hull footprint (z=0 is the ground on land, and the WATER SURFACE afloat)
frame.at_rest: every value here is at float=0, tracks=false, hatch=0. Two whole-machine z offsets ride on top of it — see FLOAT.sink and TRACKS.lift.

pivot_px._note: model z=0 projects to the pivot row in all 8 facings, at every pose

facings._note: dir 0 (N) shows the TRANSOM: the machine points away. dir 4 (S) shows the bow. Street side (-x) reads at NE E SE; curb side (+x) at SW W NW.

BODY.drive: skid steer — there is no steering axle and no articulation; a turn is counter-rotation of the two sides

collider_bbox._note: x is over the TRACKS. On the default (tired) build the widest hard point is 0.78 — the tires themselves, which sit proud of the 0.70 hull. The rack at z 1.30 is the top; without it the crown is 1.11.

mass_kg_estimate.basis: NOT measured off the rig — no rig geometry carries mass. Quoted so FLOAT.displacement has something to sit against; treat it as a gameplay knob, not a published fact.

BODY.provenance: BODIES.otter8x8 + G; hull_crown_z = crownAt(1.16); width_over_tires = 2*(wheelX 0.63 + tireW/2 0.15)

HULL._what: the tub IS the hull. One sealed poly moulding lofted through 19 stations — there is no separate frame, no bilge, no deck join. Everything in COCKPIT sits inside it.

form.bow_rocker: keel rises to 0.68 at y=1.62 over the forward 0.90 m
form.stern_tuck: keel rises to 0.34 at the transom over the aft 0.38 m
form.chine_z: bz(y) + 0.32, clamped to top-0.07 — it climbs with the bow rocker, which is why the black lower hull sweeps up forward

two_tone._note: not a decal — it is where the loft changes material, so it follows the hull form in all eight facings

HULL.provenance: hwAt/bzAt/topAt/profile() in the rig, sampled — the same functions the loft calls

FLOAT._what: THE RIG BAKES DRY. No pixel is clipped and no wake is painted. `float` only lowers the whole machine onto its waterline so the attitude is right; the GAME cuts the sprite with its own water shader. Everything the shader needs is in this section.
FLOAT.sink_formula: dz = -0.52 * float, applied to EVERY polygon (hull, tub, seats, fittings, wheels, tracks) before projection

clip_rule.plane: world z = 0 — the same plane the pivot row projects, in all eight facings
clip_rule.in_sprite_space: clip everything below the pivot row (y > 128 in a 256x192 cell). The pivot row IS the waterline whenever float > 0.
clip_rule._note: no per-facing correction: z=0 is a horizontal plane in this projection, so it is a horizontal line in the sprite too.

at_float_1._tub_note: the cockpit floor sits 0.08 m BELOW the outside water. That is correct and it is not a leak — the tub is a sealed moulding, the floor is a pan inside it. Do not drain it.
at_float_1.wheels: tires are submerged to 0.12 of their 0.64 diameter above the surface — the top 19% of each tire shows

displacement_curve._units: draft measured ABOVE the keel (add 0.24 for model z); mass in kg of fresh water displaced by the HULL ONLY
displacement_curve.excludes: the eight tires, which on the real class carry a real share of the buoyancy. Counting them would add roughly 8 x 0.045 m3 = 360 kg at full submersion — if the game wants a loaded machine to ride higher, that is where the margin is.
displacement_curve.method: trapezoidal integration of the station half-areas below the waterline, 0.02 m steps from y=-1.48 to 1.62, x2 for both sides, x1000 kg/m3

waterline_polygon_at_float_1._units: [y, half_width] at model z=0.52; mirror for -x. Use it for the wake mask, the foam ring and the hull-vs-water intersection.

downflooding._note: 0.82 m of sink is float = 1.58, outside the rig's clamped 0..1. The machine CANNOT be posed swamped. A swamping state is the game's to invent.

propulsion_afloat.means: the tires. There is no propeller, no jet, no rudder and no outboard bracket in the rig.
propulsion_afloat.steering: differential — same skid input as on land
propulsion_afloat._note: roll still animates afloat and the exposed top 19% of each tire is what the player sees turning

FLOAT.provenance: G.sinkMax, build() dz; flotation integrated off profile() — see displacement_curve.method

COCKPIT._what: an open tub with two benches, not a room. Seated occupants; the only standing space is the footwell between the benches.

footwell._note: the only clear floor. Ahead of it is the front bench pedestal, behind it the aft bench box.

obstructions._note: carries the aft bench. The rig does not model what is inside it.

helm._note: centre-steer. There is no driver's side on this machine — read that off the bar, not off the seats.

SEATS._note: ONE undivided cushion, and the helm is centred on it — which of the two riders is driving is a gameplay decision, not a rig fact
raised 0.14 m above the front cushion, on the aft box

THRESHOLD._what: THERE ARE NO DOORS. Boarding is a step over the gunwale, from either side or over the transom. Published as three ways in, not as openings.

ways_in.obstructed_by: the four tires stand 0.78 out and 0.64 tall directly under the rail — a boarder steps over a tire, not up a clear face
the four tires stand 0.78 out and 0.64 tall directly under the rail — a boarder steps over a tire, not up a clear face

ways_in._note: clear of the tires — the transom overhangs the rear axle by 0.14 m — but the rack (when fitted) stands in the way from z 0.84 to 1.30

THRESHOLD._tracked_note: tracks lift the whole machine 0.07 m, so every sill above gains 0.07

bow._what: a closed, crowned engine deck — the highest part of the hull. Not a walkable surface: it is 0.66 m wide at the crown and domed.

hatch._note: a top face — it reads at all eight facings, open or shut

aft._what: the closed transom deck. Flat enough to set a crate on; 0.34 m fore-and-aft, so nothing large.

rack.construction: tube — two side rails, two cross rails and three longitudinals at 0.30 centres. Open between the bars: small items fall through.

CARGO._no_bed: there is no cargo box, no bed and no tailgate on this machine. Anything carried rides the rack, the footwell or a rider's lap.

roll.rule: each side takes roll + its side offset. rollL = +t, rollR = -t is a spin on the spot — see YAW for the arithmetic that ties a side split to a heading change.
roll._note: no suspension anywhere on this machine. The axles are rigid, the tires ARE the suspension, and no rig param flexes them.

YAW.what: heading between the eight facings, and the ONLY yaw on this machine — there is no steer axle, so nothing turns but the whole hull. The model rotates about z before projection under a FIXED key, so the shading is rebaked for the new heading.
YAW.pivot: unaffected; the origin projects to the published pivot at any yaw
YAW.frame: yaw is a RENDER param, not geometry. Every metre in this file is in the machine frame and does not move with it — colliders, seat refs and reach points rotate with the machine as they always did.

skid_arithmetic._note: a game that yaws her without splitting the sides (or splits without yawing) will read wrong; the rig will not stop it.

YAW.afloat: yaw is independent of float. Afloat she yaws on the same tires — see FLOAT.propulsion_afloat — and the pivot row is still the waterline.
YAW.tracked: unchanged. The belt path is symmetrical, so a tracked spin uses the same arithmetic with the same 1.26 m track.

TRACKS._lift_note: the belt runs under the tires, so the WHOLE machine — hull, tub, seats, sills, rack — stands 0.07 m higher. Every z in this file gains 0.07 when tracks are fitted. Ground clearance becomes 0.31.

belt.path: stadium loop about the y=1.02 and y=-1.02 axle centres

ground_contact._note: 4.5x the tired contact patch. If soft ground, ice or bog is a gameplay surface, this is the number that should change behaviour.

TRACKS.provenance: beltPath() + buildTracks; contact = flat run 2.04 m x belt width 0.40 m x 2 sides

winch._note: a recovery point that happens to be a winch. There is no rope in the rig — the line is the game's to draw.

bimini._note: soft top on four posts. It does not fold in the rig — it is fitted or it is not.

INTERACT._note: a state change, not a place — see FLOAT. No ramp, bow door or transom gate exists to gate it.

_interact_notes.reach_point: a request, not a promise — a ground-level standing spot derived from which face the item is on. NOT validated against terrain, another vehicle, or the water's edge.
_interact_notes.visible_facings: computed, not eyeballed: a feature with outward normal n is listed for facing d when nx*sin(d*45) + ny*cos(d*45) < -0.3 (the near-side test paint() uses, edge-on excluded). Top faces read at all eight.

_excluded.CLEATS: not a boat in the harbour's sense — no mooring hardware anywhere. The winch and the bow guard are recovery points, and the sidecar says so rather than letting someone tie up to them.
_excluded.steering_geometry: no steer axle, no kingpin, no wheel yaw — correct for the class. Her steering is YAW, the whole machine, tied to the side split by the arithmetic in that section.
_excluded.suspension: there is none. Unlike the dually there is no travel param, no dz(y), and nothing for a rider to be corrected against.
_excluded.propulsion_afloat: no prop, jet, kicker bracket or rudder. See FLOAT.propulsion_afloat.
_excluded.bilge_and_drain: the tub is published as sealed. No drain plug, no scupper, no bilge pump — if the game floods it, the volume is COCKPIT.floor x depth and nothing in the rig empties it.
_excluded.wake_and_spray: the bake is dry — no wake ring, no spray, no waterline stain. FLOAT gives the polygon to draw them from.
_excluded.fuel_fill: the tank is not modelled at all. The aft box is a closed volume with nothing published inside it.
_excluded.plate_decals_mirrors: no plate, no mirrors, no aerial, no decals. At 32 px/m each is 1-3 px.
_excluded.roof_load: the bimini canopy is fabric on four posts. It is not a rack and carries nothing.
_excluded.cab: there is no enclosed cab variant in this rig. The hard-cab machines in the reference class would be a second BODIES entry.

_confirm.tub_standing: COCKPIT.footwell is 1.06 x 0.72 m of clear floor 0.42 m below the rail. Whether a player stands there (deckhand-style) or the tub is seats-only is unruled. Geometry is published either way.
_confirm.float_is_a_pose_not_a_state: the rig will hold any float 0..1 with no consequence. Whether the machine is buoyant with four riders and a loaded rack is a gameplay call — FLOAT.displacement_curve is the input, BODY.mass_kg_estimate is a guess, and nothing in the rig enforces either.
_confirm.tracked_z_shift: TRACKS.lift moves every published z by 0.07. Rider slots, reach points and sills all need it applied, and no value in this file is pre-shifted.
_confirm.transom_boarding_vs_rack: board_transom and the rack occupy the same space. The rig defaults rack:true, so on the default build the only ways in are the two sides.
_confirm.front_bench_occupancy: one 0.94 m cushion with a centred bar. Two up is the intent; the rig has no division to read and would not object to three.
_confirm.reach_points: seven, none tested against a ground collider, the tires, or each other. The side points sit 0.62 m outboard of the tires.
_confirm.yaw_and_split: YAW and the side split are published together but NOT coupled in the rig. Driving one without the other is a gameplay bug the rig cannot catch.
